input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for a few hours now. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.
Yes, I have my phone with me and I’ll do my best to follow along. Please go ahead with the first step, but if it gets too complicated, I might need a bit of extra help.
At the top of my phone’s screen, I see an airplane icon. I’m not sure what that means, but I don’t see anything about signal bars or mobile data like “4G” or “LTE.” What should I do next?
Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now at the top of my screen, it says “No Signal” and I see something about data being disabled. I don’t see any bars or “4G” or “LTE” yet. What should I do now?
It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure why that is—I haven’t taken it out or anything. What should I do now?

Alright, I’ve taken out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now, at the top of my screen, I see one bar for signal and it says “2G,” but it still says data is disabled. What should I do next?

I turned on mobile data, and now it says “2G” with one bar, and data is enabled. But I tried sending a picture message again, and it still won’t go through. Is there something else I should try? This is getting a bit frustrating.

I changed the network mode like you said, and now I see “5G” at the top with full bars and data enabled. But I tried sending a picture message again, and it still won’t send. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose my photos if we keep changing things?

I checked the APN settings like you asked. It says the APN name is “internet,” but I don’t see anything listed for the MMSC URL—it just says “Not Set.” I’m not sure what that means. What should I do next?
I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now? Will that affect my regular calls? I just want to make sure I’m doing the right thing.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really starting to worry that this will never work again.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for a few hours now. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you with your MMS issue.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Thank you for providing your information, John. I have located your account.

To help you with your MMS (picture messaging) issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few quick checks on your phone. Are you able to follow some instructions on your device right now? If so, please let me know, and I’ll walk you through the first step.
Yes, I have my phone with me and I’ll do my best to follow along. Please go ahead with the first step, but if it gets too complicated, I might need a bit of extra help.

Great! Let’s start by checking your phone’s basic connectivity and status. Please look at the top of your phone’s screen (the status bar) and let me know:

1. Do you see any airplane icon (✈️) or a message like “No Signal”?
2. What does your signal strength look like (how many bars, or does it say “4G”, “5G”, etc.)?
3. Is there a mobile data icon (like “LTE”, “4G”, “5G”, or a small “H+” or “E”)?

This will help us determine if your phone is connected to the network and if mobile data is enabled, which are both required for MMS to work. Please describe what you see.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
At the top of my phone’s screen, I see an airplane icon. I’m not sure what that means, but I don’t see anything about signal bars or mobile data like “4G” or “LTE.” What should I do next?

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is turned on, which disables all wireless connections—including cellular service and mobile data. This is why you’re unable to send MMS messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
- Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
- Tapping the airplane icon so it is no longer highlighted.

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the network. Then, check if your signal bars and mobile data icons (like “4G” or “LTE”) appear at the top of your screen.

Let me know once you’ve done this, and if you see your signal and data icons again. We’ll continue from there!

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now at the top of my screen, it says “No Signal” and I see something about data being disabled. I don’t see any bars or “4G” or “LTE” yet. What should I do now?

Thank you for the update. Since you’re seeing “No Signal” and data is disabled, let’s check if your SIM card is being recognized by your phone. This can sometimes happen if the SIM card is not properly seated.

Please check your phone’s SIM card status. On most phones, you can do this by:
- Going to your phone’s Settings.
- Looking for a section called “About Phone,” “Connections,” or “SIM Card Status.”
- Checking if it says the SIM card is “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked.”

Could you let me know what your phone says about the SIM card status? If you’re not sure how to find this, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can give you more specific instructions.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
It looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure why that is—I haven’t taken it out or anything. What should I do now?

If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, it’s possible the SIM card has become loose or isn’t making proper contact. This can happen even if you haven’t removed it.

Please try the following steps:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card tray (usually with a small pin or tool).
3. Take out the SIM card, check for any dust or debris, and gently reinsert it.
4. Place the tray back in and power your phone back on.

After your phone restarts, check if it now recognizes the SIM card and if you see signal bars or mobile data icons at the top of your screen.

Let me know what you see after doing this, and we’ll continue troubleshooting if needed.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I’ve taken out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now, at the top of my screen, I see one bar for signal and it says “2G,” but it still says data is disabled. What should I do next?

Great job reseating the SIM card! Now that your phone recognizes the SIM and you have a signal, let’s enable mobile data, which is required for MMS to work.

Please turn on mobile data by:
- Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
- Looking for the “Mobile Data” icon (it may look like two arrows or say “Data”).
- Tapping it to enable mobile data.

Once mobile data is enabled, check if you see a data icon like “2G,” “3G,” “4G,” or “LTE” at the top of your screen, and let me know if the “data disabled” message disappears.

After you’ve done this, please try sending a picture message (MMS) again and let me know if it works or if you encounter any issues.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I turned on mobile data, and now it says “2G” with one bar, and data is enabled. But I tried sending a picture message again, and it still won’t go through. Is there something else I should try? This is getting a bit frustrating.

Thank you for your patience. Since your phone is currently connected to a “2G” network with only one bar, this network type is generally too slow and unreliable for sending MMS messages. MMS requires at least a 3G, 4G, or 5G connection.

Let’s try switching your phone’s network mode to prefer higher-speed networks. Here’s what to do:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Find “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
3. Look for “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
4. Select an option like “4G/3G/2G (auto connect)” or “4G/5G preferred.”

After making this change, wait a moment to see if your phone connects to a stronger network (like “3G,” “4G,” or “LTE”) and more signal bars appear.

Once you see a better network type, try sending your picture message again. Let me know what network type you see after changing the setting, and if MMS works now. If not, we’ll continue troubleshooting.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I changed the network mode like you said, and now I see “5G” at the top with full bars and data enabled. But I tried sending a picture message again, and it still won’t send. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose my photos if we keep changing things?

You won’t lose your photos by changing these settings—your pictures are safe on your device. Thank you for following the steps so far.

Since you now have a strong “5G” connection and data is enabled, the next thing to check is your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent MMS from working, even with a good signal.

Could you please check your APN settings? On most phones, you can do this by:
- Going to Settings.
- Selecting “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
- Tapping on “Access Point Names” or “APN.”

Look for any mention of “MMSC” or “MMS” in the APN details. If you see anything that looks incorrect or missing, let me know. If you’re unsure, you can also tell me what you see listed under APN settings, and I’ll guide you from there.

Once we confirm your APN settings, we’ll know if they need to be reset. Let me know what you find!

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked the APN settings like you asked. It says the APN name is “internet,” but I don’t see anything listed for the MMSC URL—it just says “Not Set.” I’m not sure what that means. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. The missing MMSC URL is likely the reason MMS isn’t working—this setting is required for sending and receiving picture messages.

To fix this, you should reset your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. Here’s how you can do it:
1. In the APN settings menu, look for an option like “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.”
2. Tap this option to restore the correct APN and MMSC settings.

After resetting the APN settings, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Please go ahead and reset your APN settings, then restart your phone. Once your phone is back on, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works. If you need help finding the reset option, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can provide more detailed instructions.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. I understand this process can be overwhelming, and I’m here to help you through it.

Let’s try one more thing that sometimes affects MMS: Wi-Fi Calling. If Wi-Fi Calling is enabled, it can sometimes interfere with sending picture messages.

Could you please check if Wi-Fi Calling is turned on? You can usually find this by:
- Going to Settings.
- Looking for “Wi-Fi Calling” (sometimes under “Connections” or “Network & Internet”).

If Wi-Fi Calling is ON, please turn it OFF and then try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if this helps, or if you need more guidance. If this doesn’t resolve the issue, I’ll make sure you get the help you need.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now? Will that affect my regular calls? I just want to make sure I’m doing the right thing.

Yes, please go ahead and turn off Wi-Fi Calling. This will not affect your ability to make regular calls over the cellular network, especially since you now have a strong “5G” signal. Turning off Wi-Fi Calling is a safe step and can help resolve MMS issues.

After you turn off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still have trouble. If it still doesn’t work, I’ll continue to assist you.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m really starting to worry that this will never work again.

Thank you for your patience and for following all the troubleshooting steps so far. Since you have a strong signal, mobile data enabled, correct network mode, APN settings reset, and Wi-Fi Calling turned off, but MMS still isn’t working, this may require more advanced support.
